title: Maze & Pathfinding
short_description: Learn how a person, robot, or game character navigates from a start point to a destination through a grid containing obstacles using Graph BFS, Graph DFS, Depth-Limited Search, Flood Fill, A* Pathfinding, and Backtracking.

real_world_context.problem: A person, robot, or game character must navigate from a starting point to a destination through a grid containing obstacles. Engineers must find the shortest route, explore paths with a limited lookahead, map every reachable cell, guide movement with a heuristic, and enumerate all valid routes when every option must be tried.
real_world_context.why_it_matters: Pathfinding powers game characters, warehouse robots, delivery drones, and map navigation. Choosing BFS vs DFS vs A* vs backtracking decides whether the route is shortest, fast to compute, or exhaustive — and whether the agent gets stuck behind obstacles.

learning_objectives: Represent a maze or game grid as a graph using a 2D grid with obstacles.
Use Breadth-First Search (BFS) to find the shortest path from start to destination in an unweighted grid.
Use Depth-First Search (DFS) with Depth-Limited Search to explore paths without wandering forever.
Use Flood Fill to mark every reachable free cell from a starting position.
Use A* Pathfinding with a Manhattan-distance heuristic to reach the destination efficiently.
Use Backtracking to count all valid routes through the maze.
completion_message: You have completed the Maze & Pathfinding mission. You have learned how BFS finds shortest grid routes, DFS with depth limits explores safely, flood fill maps reachable areas, A* guides search with a heuristic, and backtracking enumerates every valid path for people, robots, and game characters.
